binders: n : Nat, bound separately inside each Filter.Eventually predicate and ranging asymptotically through Filter.atTop
c : Real, existentially quantified in the negated assertion
G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), bound by the predicate defining the measured graph event
v : Fin n, existentially quantified inside that graph-event predicate
hypotheses: In the excluded existential assertion, c is strictly positive: 0 < c.
The graph law is the binomial random-graph measure on Fin n with edge parameter equal to the subtype element 0 in [0,1].
The asymptotic predicates are interpreted over sufficiently large natural n via Filter.atTop.
conclusions: Eventually, the real product of the cast of the truncated predecessor n-1 and the underlying real value of the interval element 0 is at most 0.

There does not exist a positive real constant c such that, eventually in n, the probability is at least 9/10 that a graph sampled from the zero-edge-probability binomial random-graph law has some vertex v with degree at least c·log(n)/log(log(n)).
mathematical_definitions: For each n and p∈[0,1], LocalDef006 packages the binomial random-graph measure on simple graphs with vertex set Fin n and the ordinary natural-valued vertex degree.
The graph event at n and c is {G | ∃v, c·(log n/log(log n)) ≤ degree_G(v)}, with natural values cast to reals.
Measure.real converts the measure of that event to a real number before comparison with 9/10.
Real.log is totalized, so all natural n produce a formally defined logarithmic expression.
Natural subtraction is truncated, so n-1 is always a natural number.
translation.proposition_plain_english: The proposition says two things. First, for all sufficiently large natural numbers n, the real number (n-1)·0 is at most zero. Second, no positive real constant c can make it true for all sufficiently large n that a zero-edge-probability binomial random graph on n vertices has probability at least 90% of containing a vertex whose degree is at least c times log n divided by log log n.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The first conjunct is arithmetically trivial because the underlying value of the [0,1] subtype element 0 is exactly real zero, so the product is zero for every n, not merely eventually.
The random-graph parameter is exactly p=0, so the law is concentrated on the edgeless graph; this can make the probabilistic claim degenerate relative to a nonzero or n-dependent edge probability.
Because the second assertion is a negated existential, it is satisfied whenever every positive c fails the eventual probability bound; it does not provide a positive lower-bound constant.

Real.log is totalized and no hypotheses require n>1, log n>0, or log(log n)>0. Small-n singularities and sign changes are therefore absorbed into the formal definition, though eventuality may render them asymptotically irrelevant.
Division is totalized in the real field, so a zero denominator yields a formally defined value rather than an undefined expression.

Measure.real uses ENNReal.toReal; although the displayed law is intended to be a probability measure, in general this conversion maps an infinite measure value in a way that may not preserve an intuitive extended-real reading.
The existential vertex event is false when Fin n is empty, but this only affects small n and the surrounding assertion is eventual.
The probability comparison uses the real value 9/10, inferred from real division, and thus means 0.9 rather than truncated natural division.
ambiguities: The packet exposes LocalDef007 primarily through its constructor and projections rather than an explicit field declaration; its package interpretation is inferred from those supplied types and bodies.

No theorem in the packet explicitly states the support or normalization properties of SimpleGraph.binomialRandom at p=0, so concentration on the edgeless graph follows from the supplied description of independent Bernoulli edge choices rather than a displayed target hypothesis.
The two Filter.Eventually occurrences bind independent variables conventionally both named n; the target does not assert a shared cutoff between them.
The notation (LocalDef006 n 0).graphLaw.real relies on field/projection elaboration, but its intended reading as the real-valued measure of the following event is clear from the dependency types.
